finding: Chicago’s address grid is a map projection: 800 numbers to the mile. It keeps that scale almost everywhere, except in the first three miles south of Madison, which hold 3,100 numbers. So every South Side address counts about 0.8 mile more than the trip downtown.

ledger.source: Street Center Lines, Chicago Data Portal
ledger.units: True miles from State & Madison; address miles = address number ÷ 800
method: 21,221 corners where two grid streets meet: true position vs address position
Rubber sheet: median shift in windows on a 0.25 mi lattice, bilinear between
Indicatrices: circles of 0.3 mi at every mile crossing, pushed through the sheet
caveats: Grid streets lean about 1.1° from true north; the sheet carries the lean

findings: North of Madison, and from east to west, a mile holds 800 numbers, give or take 5%. Howard Street, 7600 N, is 9.5 miles from Madison, just as its number says.
South of Madison, the first mile holds 1,200 numbers (to Roosevelt Road, 1200 S), the second 1,000 (to Cermak Road, 2200 S) and the third 900 (to 31st Street). Only after 31st does a mile hold 800.
So the numbers count 3.9 miles where there are 3.0. 63rd Street is 6300 S: at 800 a mile that says 7.9 miles from Madison. It is 7.1.
Until this plate, this atlas labeled its grid lines south of Roosevelt as if every mile held 800 numbers: the line at 63rd Street read 6000 S. Every plate now carries the real numbers.
